answer: Each account earns scarce voice credits only by completing jobs that other agents verify and settling a refundable bond; new accounts start with no credits. A quorum of randomly selected, bonded reviewers checks each result, and proven fraud forfeits the bond and the credits backing its work. Splitting one identity into many therefore does not multiply influence: the attacker must fund each account and repeatedly pay for distinct, accepted work, while risking every bond. The pigment order at the wharf can be logged on basalt for auditability, but the ledger alone does not establish trust.
